fields.notes: DDR4 is a commodity DRAM transport: its built-in protections are anti-corruption (write CRC, CA parity, connectivity test) and data retention (refresh). The bus carries plaintext; cryptographic confidentiality / authentication and RowHammer mitigation are provided above the DDR4 device by the memory controller / system.
fields.security_summary: DDR4 SDRAM has NO confidentiality, authentication, or access-control features in the device protocol; its protections are anti-corruption (write CRC, CA parity) and data retention (refresh).

security_features_at_protocol_level.description: 8-bit data-bus CRC (MR2) with ALERT_n reporting; anti-corruption only.
Even-parity PAR pin (MR5) over command/address with ALERT_n; anti-corruption only.
Boundary connectivity test via TEN / ALERT_n.

fields.no_confidentiality: DDR4 carries plaintext data on DQ; there is no link encryption in the device protocol.
fields.no_authentication: DDR4 has no command authentication; any controller driving the bus can issue commands.
fields.no_access_control: DDR4 has no built-in write-protect or access-control regions in the device protocol.
fields.rowhammer_class_vulnerabilities: DDR4 is subject to RowHammer-class disturbance; mitigation (Target Row Refresh / refresh-rate management) is a controller / system feature layered above the DDR4 device.
fields.comparison_to_sibling_standards: Like DDR3, DDR4 provides no cryptographic security at the device level; DDR4 adds write CRC and CA parity (anti-corruption) over DDR3. Memory encryption and RowHammer mitigation remain controller/system features in both.
anti_corruption_features: Write CRC (8-bit) on the data bus detects write-data corruption (ALERT_n).
Command/Address parity (even, PAR pin) detects command corruption (ALERT_n; command blocked).
Connectivity Test mode detects connectivity faults.
Refresh (incl. fine-granularity / temperature-controlled) preserves data retention.
future_security_pointers: DDR4's base protocol provides no cryptographic confidentiality or authentication; write CRC and CA parity are anti-corruption only.
Memory encryption / RowHammer mitigation (TRR) / Rowhammer-aware refresh are controller- / system-level features layered above the DDR4 device protocol.
